title: Why Naysayers Will Never Be Good At Classroom Management
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin addresses the recurring wave of skeptics and excuse-makers he encounters in comment sections and email, who dismiss evidence of well-behaved classrooms as anomalies, staged, or the product of unrepeatable natural talent. He illustrates this with a specific counter-example, a 61-year-old teacher named Marta who commands 34 middle schoolers using SCM principles, whom naysayers would dismiss as an anomaly rather than update their beliefs. His central claim is that disbelief itself is what dooms these teachers to careers of stress and dissatisfaction, since it is easier to blame parents, administration, or smartphones than to acquire real knowledge and skill. Despite his sharp tone toward cynics, he extends an explicit invitation for any struggling or skeptical teacher to test the SCM approach starting with its foundational resources, arguing that success is available to anyone willing to take responsibility rather than assign blame.
points: Naysayers dismiss real counter-evidence, like a 61-year-old teacher commanding 34 middle schoolers, as an anomaly rather than updating their beliefs.
Linsin argues disbelief itself, not external circumstance, is what dooms skeptical teachers to a career of stress and dissatisfaction.
The specific behaviors that need to change are named directly: finger-pointing, excuse-making, and blaming parents, administration, or technology.
Despite the confrontational tone toward cynics, the piece ends with an explicit invitation for skeptics to test the approach for themselves.
quotes: The naysayers. The doubters. The excuse-makers. Pointing the finger at everyone and every thing but themselves.
You could introduce them to Marta, 61 years old and, after learning the SCM approach, under total command of her 34 middle school students.
Sadly, their disbelief dooms them. It dooms them to a career of stress, dissatisfaction, and martyrdom.

But it’s all a lie. Yes, there are challenges, including those above. But the truth is that with the right knowledge, and discipline to follow a proven set of principles and strategies, the challenges can be overcome.
Take responsibility. And with it, the control to chart a new destiny.
